explain.reason: As the main sensing and collision-avoidance module of an M1/N1 AEBS, the radar determines compliance with system-level collision detection, warning, braking and failure-monitoring requirements, although approval is granted to the vehicle rather than the radar separately.

The powered electronic radar module must meet applicable electromagnetic emission and immunity requirements, particularly because electromagnetic disturbance could affect its safety-related braking function.
The radar's automatic-braking request interface must be integrated with the M1/N1 braking system without compromising required braking operation or fault safety.

The network-connected radar and its safety-critical software must be covered by the vehicle cybersecurity assessment and applicable technical mitigations against compromised software, sensor information or braking-request communications.
The front-mounted radome and bracket must be accounted for in pedestrian-impact compliance because their stiffness and clearance behind the emblem can affect deformation of the impacted front end.
For vehicles within its application scope, the radar assembly's packaging behind the front emblem must preserve the pedestrian-impact performance addressed by the GTR's front-end impact tests.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): If the vehicle permits updates affecting this radar, the module and its software must support applicable update-integrity, compatibility and continued type-approval compliance requirements.
Although it addresses AEBS, its scope covers M2, M3, N2 and N3 rather than the specified M1/N1 vehicles; UN R152 is the relevant light-vehicle regulation.
The radar and its radome are specified as being behind the front emblem, not as exposed exterior surfaces or projections; no externally accessible radar projection is established.
The optical collision warning communicated through the instrument cluster is not an exterior lighting or light-signalling installation, and the specification contains no such lamp installation.
Emergency collision warning and braking do not constitute an ALKS, and no sustained automated lateral and longitudinal driving function is specified.
The specified emergency intervention does not establish a Driver Control Assistance System providing sustained assistance with lateral and longitudinal vehicle control.
The product directly matches the scope covering aftermarket replacement airbag modules and replacement steering wheels with airbags for M1 and N1 vehicles.
The rim, spokes, hub and splined connection form part of the manual steering equipment and must preserve its required safety and steering performance.
The electrically initiated airbag assembly and its connections perform a safety-related electrical function whose electromagnetic compatibility must be addressed.
The replacement driver airbag forms part of the protective system determining frontal-impact restraint performance for N1 vehicles and M1 vehicles within the regulation's 3,500 kg mass limit.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): The replacement airbag and steering wheel affect frontal-collision occupant-protection results where the intended vehicle falls within the regulation's mass-limited scope.

No networked controller, communications interface or cybersecurity-relevant functionality is specified in the replacement assembly; connection to the existing airbag control unit alone does not establish component-specific cybersecurity requirements.
No software or software-update capability is specified for the replacement wheel or airbag module.
The assembly does not contain a steering lock or other device preventing unauthorized use, and modification of such a device is not stated.
The steering wheel and driver airbag are interior equipment, not external projections of an M1 vehicle.
A horn switch does not bring the assembly within requirements for vehicle sound emissions during normal driving, and airbag deployment noise is not the regulated driving-noise function.
The dedicated vehicle-alarm regulation covers the alarm's detection, acoustic and optical signalling, setting and unsetting, and integration into the M1 vehicle.
Its vehicle-alarm provisions cover this permanently fitted M1 alarm and its integration, providing an alternative approval framework to UN R163 rather than requiring duplicate approval.
The electronic alarm assembly must meet applicable electromagnetic emission and immunity requirements as vehicle electrical/electronic equipment.
Using the direction indicators for the optical alarm must respect the vehicle lighting installation and electrical-connection requirements.
The direction-indicator lamps used by the alarm remain subject to the consolidated light-signalling device approval requirements.
The CAN-connected alarm ECU must be addressed in the M1 vehicle's cybersecurity assessment and implement applicable technical risk mitigations.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): If the alarm ECU supports software updates, applicable update integrity, compatibility and safe-execution requirements can constrain its design and integration.
Direction indicators are relevant, but UN R148 expressly consolidates UN R6 and is selected instead.
Setting the alarm through central locking does not make it a device preventing unauthorized vehicle use through locking steering, transmission or equivalent driving mechanisms.
The specification expressly excludes engine immobilization and identifies the immobilizer as a separate system.
The dashboard status LED is not a standardized LED light source intended for an approved vehicle lamp, and the direction-indicator light-source technology is unspecified.
This regulation addresses vehicle sound during normal driving, not the acoustic performance of a security-alarm siren.

The 50 mm microprismatic contour-marking tape falls within retro-reflective marking materials, requiring compliance with the applicable Class C optical, colour, dimensional, durability and approval-marking requirements.

Full contour markings applied to the sides and rear of an O4 semi-trailer must satisfy the applicable conspicuity-marking installation requirements, including colour, positioning, extent and visibility.
Its retro-reflective marking provisions are consolidated into UN R150, so UN R150 is selected instead under the consolidation rule.
The product is contour-marking material rather than a discrete retro-reflector, and UN R3 is also consolidated into UN R150.
The tape is a passive retro-reflective marking, not a light-signalling lamp such as a side-marker or end-outline marker lamp.
The specified film and adhesive contain no electrical or electronic devices that would trigger electromagnetic-compatibility requirements.
Although applied externally, the tape is fitted to an O4 trailer, whereas this regulation covers external projections of M1 vehicles.

The EPS column forms part of the M1 vehicle's steering equipment, so its assistance performance, mechanical transmission and behaviour following electrical or electronic faults must support compliance with steering-system requirements.
The motor, sensors and CAN-connected ECU constitute an electrical/electronic assembly whose electromagnetic emissions and immunity must meet applicable EMC requirements.
Vehicle-level cybersecurity approval requires risks involving the safety-relevant, CAN-connected EPS controller to be assessed and addressed through appropriate technical protections.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): For an M1 vehicle within the regulation's mass scope, the column's collapse behaviour and integration affect frontal-impact occupant protection and steering-control displacement.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): For an M1 vehicle within the regulation's mass scope, the collapsible column affects compliance with full-width frontal-impact occupant-protection requirements.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): If the EPS control software is updateable, vehicle-level software-update requirements constrain the compatibility, integrity and safe execution of updates affecting steering assistance.
The specified 12 V steering-assistance motor is not an electric propulsion system or traction-energy storage system.
No steering lock or other device preventing unauthorized vehicle use is specified; a steering column alone does not establish this function.
The component is neither an aftermarket airbag module nor a replacement steering wheel equipped with an airbag.
The specification expressly excludes automated steering and does not include an Automated Lane Keeping System.
Driver-commanded power assistance alone is not a Driver Control Assistance System, and no automated lateral or longitudinal control function is specified.
The LED front fog lamp must meet the consolidated requirements for front-fog-lamp photometry, colour, durability, plastic lenses, LED modules and approval markings.
The paired front fog lamps on an M1 vehicle are subject to installation requirements covering position, visibility, orientation, aiming and electrical switching.

The integrated electronic LED driver and its connection to the vehicle supply bring the lamp assembly within the applicable electromagnetic-compatibility requirements for electrical/electronic subassemblies.
The exposed lamp surfaces and any accessible housing or mounting edges must satisfy the applicable external-projection requirements when integrated into the M1 vehicle's front fascia.

The lower-front lamp assembly, including its rigid heat sink and mounting bracket, must be integrated without compromising applicable pedestrian-impact performance in the vehicle's tested front-end areas.
The lower-front lamp construction can affect the pedestrian leg-impact performance addressed by this GTR, which provides technical requirements rather than a separate UNECE component approval.

The lamp's lower-front-fascia integration must support compliance with the applicable lighting-function, visibility and adjustment requirements following the prescribed low-speed protective-device impacts.
Although directly concerned with front fog lamps, its requirements are consolidated into UN R149, which is selected instead.
It covers standardised LED light-source categories; the specification instead describes a non-replaceable soldered LED module, with no standardised source category identified.
The lamp contains neither a filament light source nor a standardised LED replacement for a filament source.
Its scope expressly excludes glazing for lighting and light-signalling devices, so the polycarbonate lamp lens is not safety glazing under this regulation.
The specified device performs front fog road illumination, not any of the light-signalling functions covered by UN R148.
The non-original replacement silencer for an L3 motorcycle falls directly within this regulation, which governs its noise performance, construction, durability and approval markings.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): If the motorcycle has a positive-ignition engine, the replacement silencer must preserve applicable vehicle gaseous-emissions compliance because changed exhaust flow resistance can affect emissions despite retaining the catalyst and engine settings.
Although it concerns vehicle noise, its scope covers categories M and N, not the specified L3 motorcycle.
The silencer is not a replacement catalytic converter or other pollution-control device, and the specified L3 motorcycle is outside the referenced UN R83 vehicle categories.
Its external-projection requirements apply to M1 passenger cars, not L3 motorcycles, despite the silencer's exposed mounting.
The specified silencer is entirely passive and contains no electrical or electronic devices that would trigger electromagnetic-compatibility requirements.
The component contains no lighting devices, and the specification identifies no lamp relocation or obstruction that would bring lighting-installation requirements into this assessment.
The rear bumper's beam, crash boxes and energy absorber contribute directly to the M1 vehicle's required performance in low-speed protective-device collision tests.
The steel rear cross-member, crash boxes and absorber form part of the structure whose performance determines the M1 vehicle's behaviour in a rear-end collision.
The exposed bumper fascia, diffuser, covers and integrated devices must satisfy the applicable external-projection requirements for M1 vehicles.
The two Class IA retro-reflectors fall expressly within this consolidated regulation's scope and must meet its applicable optical, colour, durability and marking requirements.
The bumper must position and orient the rear retro-reflectors to satisfy the applicable M1 installation requirements, including geometric visibility and mounting location.
The powered ultrasonic sensors and their electrical connections must satisfy the applicable electromagnetic-compatibility requirements as electronic equipment integrated into the vehicle.

verworfen (nur Fahrzeugebene): The sensor-to-ECU interface must be considered within the M1 vehicle's cybersecurity risk assessment and applicable mitigations, although this is vehicle-level approval rather than separate bumper approval.
The reflectors are relevant, but UN R150 consolidates UN R3 and is selected instead under the consolidation rule.
Its pedestrian-impact requirements concern the vehicle's front-end impact zones, not the specified rear bumper.
Its pedestrian headform and legform impact requirements concern front-end pedestrian protection rather than this rear bumper.
The assembly contains passive retro-reflectors, not any of the light-signalling lamps covered by this regulation.
Software updates are not specified for either the supplied sensors or their associated ECU, so the stated electrical connection alone does not establish applicability.

The system directly performs the safety-belt reminder function covered by this regulation, including detection of unfastened belts and staged visual and audible warnings for the M1 vehicle's seating positions.
The electrically powered sensors, body-control-unit evaluation and warning outputs must satisfy applicable electromagnetic emission and immunity requirements.
verworfen (nur Fahrzeugebene): The M1 vehicle's cybersecurity assessment and management must account for the electronically implemented reminder function and its body-control-unit integration.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): If the vehicle permits software updates affecting the reminder function, those updates must be covered by the vehicle's applicable software-update approval and management provisions.
The instrument-cluster and overhead-console tell-tales are interior driver warnings, not the exterior lighting or light-signalling devices whose installation this regulation governs.
Using vehicle speed to escalate warnings and displaying tell-tales in the instrument cluster does not make the reminder a speedometer or odometer.
The specified system warns about belt use but does not provide crash restraint or control a protective system; no influence on frontal-impact restraint performance is stated.
The audible warning concerns unfastened safety-belts, not a vehicle alarm system protecting against unauthorized intrusion or use.
Interior reminder tell-tales are not standardized LED light sources intended for use in approved lamps within this regulation's scope.

The laminated windscreen requires safety-glazing approval covering mechanical and optical performance, identification and marking, together with compliance with the regulation's vehicle-installation provisions.
The externally exposed windscreen perimeter and plastic edge trim must satisfy the applicable external-projection requirements for M1 vehicles.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): Where the prescribed pedestrian headform test area extends onto the windscreen, its glass construction and bonded support affect the head-impact performance that the M1 vehicle must achieve.
verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): The windscreen construction and its bonded boundary affect pedestrian head-impact performance wherever included in the GTR's applicable headform test area.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): For a vehicle within the regulation's mass scope, the bonded windscreen and adhesive joint form part of the frontal-impact assembly whose deformation and occupant-protection performance must comply.

verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): For an M1 vehicle within the regulation's mass scope, the bonded windscreen's contribution to occupant-compartment behaviour must be accounted for in demonstrating frontal-impact occupant protection.
The windscreen explicitly has no heating wires, antennas or other electrical functions, so it is not an electrical/electronic subassembly requiring EMC compliance.
The windscreen contains no lighting or light-signalling device whose installation this regulation would govern.
No windscreen-mounted AEBS camera, sensor optical path or emergency-braking function is specified; the mirror base alone does not establish such an integration.
This passive glazing assembly has no specified electronic interface or cybersecurity function, although the vehicle manufacturer may have independent obligations under the regulation.
The windscreen contains no software or software-update capability, so this regulation imposes no identified requirement on its design or installation.
